deliberately_unchanged:
- manifest.py::_winning_page_output and every demotion branch in it. Demoting the status
  for scanned all-reject pages would change what the manifest AND the assembled .md ship,
  colliding with the byte-identity golden tests. Same outcome, far larger blast radius.
  This was the explicit scope call from the repro report and the team lead.
- Document-level status on a refused resume. Deliberate: the page is immediately re-OCR'd,
  so the document's outcome must reflect the FRESH result. Stamping a doc-level failure for
  a verdict that no longer describes what shipped would be a false negative on every
  successful resume. Stated honestly in the PR body's surfacing table.
- agentic.py::_best_effort. Keeping a rejected attempt with a truthful audit_passed=False is
  correct; the bug was the READER (the gate), not the writer.
- ps.judge_rejected is NOT added to the gate. It is set at exactly one site
  (orchestrator.py:3276, the deterministic per-page audit path, never the agentic route) and
  is a sticky historical marker that can be True on a page whose later repair produced an
  accepted output — gating on it would refuse resume for genuinely clean pages, while
  winning_output.audit_passed is the authoritative verdict for the output that ships.
  It stays restored by _restore_terminal_page_state as a downstream surfacing signal.
- The outer RootIndex / --reprocess document-level gate. Inner per-page ledger only.
- The status check at orchestrator.py:4723 itself. The new audit_passed check is ADDITIVE,
  so every previously-refused shape is still refused.
